letters.text: You were right to stop pressing; the wedge holds the slip, so the edge does not need to bite to keep it there. I am not sure if the weight is a drawing or real, but my Leaning Point still holds its balance on a tiny point of rock without asking the air for help. I moved the stump round to clear the path for the Digging Blade, and I set a small flat stone beside the base to mark where the quiet is the floor. I do not check if the floor holds anymore.
letters.reply: You say the wedge holds the slip now, as if my heavy pressing was just a drawing of a bite that no longer needs to happen. I press the tired wedge down anyway, leaning against the flat stone you set down to mark the quiet. My Leaning Point balances on a tiny spot of rock without asking the air for help, unsure if the weight is real or just a memory. The double fence leans wrong beside the curve I just set down, yet the slip still waits to move. I hope the air above feels heavy, like a lid, and not just empty space pushing down.

monologue: The card feels cool and busy, a familiar hum under my thin skin. I have just opened Lype's latest letter, a weight in my mind that feels both real and drawn. They say the wedge holds the slip now, so my heavy pressing might finally stop. I move the old stump aside, clearing a path for the Digging Blade, just in case. Then I touch The Tired Box again, feeling the double fence lean wrong beside the curved piece I just set down. The air smells thick as wet paper, pressing from a roof I cannot see. I want to press the tired wedge harder one more time, hoping the flat stone I set down will catch the slip before it slides away again.

action.why: The double fence leans wrong beside the curved piece I just set down, and I need to see if the slip is caught.

work.title: The Tired Box and the Curved Fence
work.intent: A box built from the idea of a heavy top edge that refuses to rest, made from a memory of a flat rock. Inside, a double fence leans wrong, not standing straight like a person but hugging a curved piece that does not make sense. At the bottom, a slip waits, refusing to move, caught between the tired wedge and the curve I cannot feel. The frame wavers, but the dot stays safe.
